items.title: The 'extraordinarily unusual' factor in Russia's war on Ukraine
items.description: For the first time since its invasion of Ukraine, Russia has lost troops faster than it can replace them. It's one of many grim milestones of a bloody war that has now been going for four years.

items.title: LGBTQIA+ teens bashed and filmed in IS-inspired Sydney attacks
items.description: An ABC investigation has obtained distressing videos and victims' accounts of IS sympathisers hunting and bashing gay and bisexual boys on camera in Sydney.

items.title: 'ISIS bride' was 14 when she married a terrorist, sister says
items.description: The sister of an Australian woman who married an Islamic State fighter has revealed how her sister was "groomed" into travelling to a war zone in Syria, where she is now stuck.

items.title: How an 'entitled' Perth obstetrician's drunken behaviour ruined multiple lives
items.description: Sought-after obstetrician Rhys Bellinge appeared to have it all — but that changed in an instant when his drunken, high-speed driving killed a young university graduate and left a rideshare driver with permanent injuries.

items.title: 250 NSW officers equipped with long-arm rifles to form rapid respond unit
items.description: More than 200 police officers equipped with long-arm rifles will be deployed to places of worship, major events and mass gatherings like protests on a risk basis.

items.title: Live: Call to turn temperature down after 'very troubling' threat on PM's residence
items.description: A Labor frontbencher has repeated a call for the temperature to be lowered after the prime minister's "very troubling" evacuation from The Lodge last night. Follow live.

items.title: Two arrested in alleged kidnapping murder of Sydney man Chris Baghsarian
items.description: The arrests come less than 24 hours after police discovered human remains near a golf club in Sydney's north-west.

items.title: Could one surgeon undo decades of advocacy for endometriosis?
items.description: Endometriosis sufferers have been left "sick" and reeling over the findings of a months-long ABC investigation into a Melbourne gynaecologist.

items.title: Gold Coast Trump Tower developer was 'uncontactable' after business collapse
items.description: The businessman behind a proposed Trump Tower on the Gold Coast ran a development business that collapsed owing $28 million.

items.title: Iran signs $700 million arms deal with Russia, reports say
items.description: Iran has reportedly signed a secret arms deal with Russia to acquire thousands of advanced shoulder-fired missiles to help boost its air defences.

items.title: Live: Software firm WiseTech to slash 2,000 jobs due to AI
items.description: WiseTech will slash jobs over the next 18 months, while the cost of remediating underpaid staff has hit Woolworths's profit. Inflation data for January is due at 11.30am AEDT. Follow the latest updates in our live blog.

items.title: Outback residents 'dancing in the rain' as February record breaks
items.description: Dry red dirt turns to flowing rivers and lakes as heavy rainfall breaks a century-old record in Mount Isa.

items.title: Wittenoom traditional owners launch $1.5 billion compensation claim
items.description: Banjima traditional owners say the thousands of hectares left poisoned by decades of asbestos mining have caused one of the highest death rates of mesothelioma in the world.

items.title: Antisemitism royal commission facing 'limitations'
items.description: The antisemitism royal commission is underway, but it faces some real tests in delivering justice to those impacted in the wake of the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: 'I just burst into tears': 400yo viola found after a five-year search
items.description: The instrument is believed to be one of the finest tenor violas in existence and the only surviving example of its kind.

items.title: Pastry stall sells 650kg of knafeh in first three days of Ramadan
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attended the opening night of the Ramadan night market in Melbourne's Dandenong, which organisers hope will attract at least a million people over the course of the holy month.

items.title: Travel quiz: Can you win our race around the world?
items.description: Which European city is home to the Rijksmuseum? And which dance style is Argentina best known for?

items.title: 'She's screaming': Court hears husband recount wife's horrific 1999 murder
items.description: A jury has watched hospital footage of Irma Palasics's husband describing the night she was killed in 1999, as two men stand trial over her death.

items.title: What to know about new passport requirements for British dual citizens starting today
items.description: Your guide to the dual citizen entry requirements for the UK that are coming into effect today.

items.title: UK backs release of 'arrogant' ex-prince Andrew's trade envoy documents
items.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested last week on suspicion of misconduct in public office amid claims he shared confidential government information with Jeffrey Epstein.

items.title: Alice Springs citizenship ceremonies no longer to be held on January 26
items.description: The Alice Springs Town Council has passed a motion to move citizenship ceremonies, traditionally held on January 26, to an alternative date. It comes after the mayor decided not to take part in formal council Australia Day events earlier this year.

items.title: Albanese asked to 'urgently rescind' appointment of NT administrator
items.description: Politicians, advocates and civil society leaders have made a last-ditch plea for Anthony Albanese to intervene ahead of the swearing-in of controversial incoming NT administrator David Connolly.

items.title: Council's 'exorbitant' travel bill $46k higher than disclosed
items.description: Gold Coast councillors question undisclosed staff travel costs after an extra $46,000 in spending is revealed, prompting calls for greater transparency and oversight.

items.title: How a football tackle almost ended up with a leg amputation
items.description: A catastrophic footy injury during a Melbourne reserves game changed Connor Rogers's life in an instant. In the aftermath, the support of his local footy club helped him recover and showed him the power of community. WARNING: This article contains graphic imagery.

items.title: How Han Xu has taken the WNBL by storm
items.description: The Perth Lynx were a middling side after eight games of the WNBL season, but the arrival of Han Xu sparked an astonishing turnaround in their fortunes — both on and off the court.
